detail:
Peer-reviewed orthopaedic guidance by Ericson and Wolman (2017) describes braces and splints as providing external joint stabilization that is useful after flare-ups and during the early stages of rehabilitation. They describe special-purpose finger splints as "particularly effective" for swan-neck hyperextension of the finger PIP joints and for the thumb CMC/MP joints. For ankle stability they discuss foot orthotics and supportive footwear such as laced boots with arch support.

A critical caveat runs through both the Ehlers-Danlos Society and the orthopaedic review: splints are not a substitute for muscle strengthening, and consistent use "can make muscles weaker through disuse." The review also notes limited evidence supporting long-term splint use for the hand and wrist.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor or occupational therapist about whether a brace or splint fits your situation.
sourceName: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part C (Ericson & Wolman, 2017)
sourceVideoTitle: Orthopedic management of patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndromes
